Breakfast Club
At both of our sites we provide a breakfast club which is run by the staff in our school to support working parents. This helps to build positive relationships for the children as they are already familiar with our staff. Children also enjoy meeting and playing with children from different year groups, building relationships through the board games and activities on offer. We encourage the children to become independent from an early age, by helping themselves to breakfast, taking responsibility for their belongings at the end of the session and helping to tidy up. The breakfast is provided by the school and the children can enjoy a range of healthy breakfast items daily at the cost of £6.00 per day. Payments must be made in advance on-line via School Gateway Breakfast club runs daily from 7.45am – 9.00am.
To book a place at our breakfast club, please log onto school gateway where you will be able to book and pay for your sessions. If your preference is to pay by childcare vouchers, you will need to contact the school office to make your booking. If you would like any more information about breakfast club or need to make any amendments please email our staff using breakfastclub@henrycavendish.co.uk.

Special Educational Needs (SEND)
Special Educational Needs and Disability (SEND)
All Lambeth maintained schools have a similar approach to meeting the needs of pupils with Special Educational Needs and are supported by the Local Authority to ensure that all pupils, regardless of their specific needs, make the best possible progress in school. All schools are supported to be as inclusive as possible, with the needs of pupils with a Special Educational Need/s and or Disabilities being met in a mainstream setting wherever possible, where families want this to happen. The school will meet the needs of children with the following SEND: • Communication and interaction • Cognition and learning • Social, mental and emotional health • Sensory /physical
The information in our SEND report (link below) details the offer within the school and ways in which parents, children and young people may access the support required.

Admissions Nursery - Application process
Prospective Parents
Admissions Nursery - Application process
Application process for Nursery places at Henry Cavendish
At Henry Cavendish children are eligible to start nursery in the intake following their third birthday. We have an intake every September, sometimes in January and very occasionally in April. An intake in January or April is dependent on class numbers at the time, and so these do not happen every year.
If you would like to add your details to the interest list for the nursery at Henry Cavendish Balham or Streatham, please click on the relevant link below:
-Nursery Interest form - DOB: September 2023 - August 2024
-Nursery Interest form - DOB: September 2024 - August 2025
If your child's date of birth is between September 2022 - August 2023, please refer to the Nursery - September 2026 page.
Once you complete the form and submit your details your child will be registered on our interest list. It is worth noting that our interest list is not an application or a waiting list.
We will ​email information ​a​nd instructions on how to apply for a place in our nursery as follows:
September start - 3rd birthday falls between January and August - we will email in the Spring, by March.
January start - 3rd birthday falls between September and December - we will email in the Autumn, by October.
April start - 3rd birthday falls between January and March - we will email early in the Spring by, January/February.
Should you have any questions or queries about our nursery or the admissions process, or you would like to book a tour, please do not hesitate to contact us on 020 8673 3376 or admissions@henrycavendish.co.uk.
We look forward to welcoming you and your child to Henry Cavendish!

Inclusion: SEN, EAL, More Able
At Henry Cavendish we believe that all pupils have a common entitlement to a broad, balanced, creative and relevant academic and social curriculum, and to be fully included in all aspects of school life. We believe that educational inclusion is about equal opportunities for all pupils. This does not mean that we treat all pupils in the same way, but that we respond to pupils in ways which take account of their varied life experiences and needs. We strive to eliminate prejudice and discrimination, and to develop a safe, healthy environment where all pupils can flourish and develop the skills to continue as lifelong learners.
We recognise the crucial role played by parents, carers and families in improving outcomes for pupils, and the important role of the local community. We aim to develop the whole child, ensuring that they become self-confident, flexible, inquisitive learners who are emotionally literate, self-aware and happy members of the school community.

Early Years Foundation Stage - Reception Class
At Henry Cavendish Balham and Streatham we have one intake and all children will join the Reception class in September. All applications must be submitted online using via Pan London admissions. The applications process can start from the beginning of October and the deadline to submit your application is normally 15th January. All applications for a place in the Reception class must be made through the eAdmissions website (Pan London).
Parents will be notified via text and email towards the middle of April of the school place their child has been offered. Henry Cavendish is a Lambeth community school and therefore you do not have to complete any supplementary forms.
Selection criteria for a place in our Reception Class:
Criterion 1 -Children with Exceptional Medical or Social Needs
Criterion 2 - Looked After Children
Criterion 3 - Siblings
Criterion 4 - Children of staff
Criterion 5 – Distance
Once you have been offered a place in our Reception class you will be invited to a short but important meeting. The meeting will outline what happens in a school day, you will meet staff who work at the school and staff will be on hand to answer any questions you may have.
It is not necessary for your child to attend this meeting, as we will hold stay and play sessions for both you and your child at the beginning of term before they start school full time.
If you are offered a place at our Reception and you are new to the school (your child has not previously attended our nursery class), we will arrange a home visit before your child starts. Home visits will last approximately 30 – 45 minutes and you will be visited by one of our teaching staff who will be accompanied by an Early Years Educator.
During a home visit staff will:
1. Talk to you and your child
2. Complete the Pre Entry Forms
3. Answer any questions or concerns you may have
4. Confirm the date when your child will start
We welcome all parents to come and tour our school to see how we do things. The tours are carried out by a member of our Senior Leadership Team and last approximately 45 to 60 minutes. You will be among either 3 or 4 sets of other parents. If you would like to come and have a look around either of our sites please contact the school office and they will be able to give you the next available dates. Telephone: 020 8673 3376 or email admissions@henrycavendish.co.uk.

French Curriculum Intent
Our curriculum will represent, value and celebrate the diverse society in which we live
Our French curriculum is enriched with music and celebrations from around the world to allow children to expand their understanding of the diversity that exists within the Francophone community, foster their curiosity and help deepen their understanding of the world beyond a stereotypical image. Learning a second language will also offer pupils the opportunity to explore relationships between language and identity, develop a deeper understanding of other cultures and the world around them with a better awareness of self, others and cultural differences.
All children will develop into confident, articulate communicators.
Our French curriculum aims at providing children with the confidence and necessary skills to converse, read and write in French and develop intercultural understanding. Our ambition is for pupils to develop a love of languages, expand their horizons to other countries, cultures and people and help them grow into curious, confident and reflective language learners. which in return will equip them with a strong foundation for further language studies.
All children will be challenged.
Being challenged in French fosters children’s enjoyment of and engagement with the subject. We introduce ideas or concepts at early stages where appropriate and ensure that topics, when revisited, are taught at a progressively more challenging level. Wherever possible, learning is presented in a way that enables children to explore.
The topic and content of our Curriculum will be varied, immersive and engaging.
At the heart of our French Curriculum is the desire to expose children to authentic French language and experiences. We provide a breadth of learning experiences in every year group, to build on the interests and skills of all children. Using a range role play scenarios, our pupils learn how to apply their skills in different contexts. In each sequence of learning, pupils are provided with opportunities to work collaboratively and be active participants and agents of their own learning.
All children will use their creativity.
In French, our pupils are empowered to make choices about their learning and pursue lines of enquiry. They are encouraged to research language they are unsure of and make use of banks of reference materials to help with their spoken and written language, therefore building on their prior knowledge.
All children will become happy, empathetic and confident citizens.
Our aim is to create a safe learning environment in which pupils ask questions, share their understanding of the language, give feedback to their peers and share their cultural identity. Following our school’s Rights Respecting Ethos, children are expected to be mindful and respectful when working collaboratively. Both children and adults create an environment appreciative to the fact that we can all learn from one another. A collaborative work ethic allows views and opinions to be valued, respected and acknowledged. Our ambition is for children to leave Henry Cavendish as open-minded, active, proud and positive global citizens.
